Hi Stephanie,

Hope you had a good weekend. We just finished our internal forecast and wanted to start the renewal conversation early. Good news: we like Redwood and want to extend for two years. The caveat: our finance team is concerned about the headline rate increases they’re seeing across cloud vendors for 2028.

Two asks from our side:
- Can we lock a capped effective rate for 24 months?
- We need flexibility for usage variance — Q3–Q4 2027 looks volatile, and we don’t want to prepay a fixed amount that we can’t use.

Would a multi-year prepay with some form of flexible tranche help? Open to a hybrid approach (fixed upfront tranche + seasonal top-ups). Please share a quick sketch of options and any impact on discounting.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan — great to hear you want to extend. We can definitely design something that both locks a favorable rate and gives you runway for usage swings. High-level option I recommend: a "flex tranche" structure. Quick sketch below.

Summary (high level):
- Term: 24 months (2028–2029).
- Core tranche: 60% of expected annual spend prepaid at contract signing. This tranche gets the largest tiered discount (example: 18% off list).
- Flex tranche(s): two seasonal tranches (Q1 and Q3 optional top-ups) representing up to 25% additional prepaid credits that you can buy at a smaller discount (e.g., 8–10%) within predefined windows. Unused flex credits roll forward within the term but expire at end of contract.
- Usage safeguard: monthly reconciliation; if actual usage exceeds prepaid + flex, on-demand rates apply but we propose a cap (max 30% above prepaid blended rate) to avoid surprise invoices.
- Ramp schedule: Year 1 prepaid covers 70% of first-year expected usage; Year 2 automatically reduces prepaid floor to 50% unless you choose to re-up flex tranches.
- Other: SLA credit guardrails, carry-forward rules for unused credits, and reporting cadence.

I attached a one-page term sketch (Redwood_FlexTranche_TermSheet_v1.pdf). If this looks directionally right I’ll loop in Ben for pricing authority and Marissa for renewal logistics and DocuSign flow.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short 20-min call to walk through the mechanics.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Steph — sounds reasonable. Pricing guardrails we can commit to today:
- Core tranche (>= 60% prepaid): up to 18% discount off hosted list for US region, subject to standard volume tiers.
- Flex tranche (seasonal top-ups within windows): 8% discount, with a cap at 12% for large topping events (>$250k).
- Surge cap: agree to a blended cap no higher than 30% above the prepaid blended rate for truly unexpected over-usage; this is intended as a safety valve, not a replacement for proper capacity planning.
- Legal: standard payment terms (Net30) and credits handled via usage ledger; unused core credits can roll forward up to 6 months into Year 2, flex credits expire at end of term.

Request from my side: include a one-sentence SLA exception clause for prepayment disputes and get Finance sign-off if they want longer carry-forward.

I’ve penciled DW-2027-RNWL-003 in my tracker — we can present a tidy term sheet once Jordan confirms direction.

Ben Carter
Head of Deal Operations, Redwood Inference
